title: Mom's questions
lede: Everything Nicholas still needs from you, in one place. The first pages were answered on September 9; this is what's left. Each part sends itself to Nicholas a few seconds after you stop typing and keeps a copy on your phone.

sections.title: 1. Upper Deck website (what's left)
sections.lead: Two questions; the rest were answered on September 9.

qs.t: Anything you would change in Veronica's answers?
qs.w: She ruled on September 9: $250 counted after quantity discounts (never shipping) and $75 for showroom pickup · no card taken on the website, charged once when the order ships, net-30 accounts by check · every Min. item: the minimum, then any number · orders sync into the office system (LMS, backup VXP) · no one sees prices or orders until approved · hours Mon–Thu 8–3 · keep the checkout pickup switch, drop the cart question.

sections.title: 2. Moby Dick website (what's left)
sections.lead: Two questions; the first ten were answered on September 9.

qs.t: Who is approved to buy from Moby Dick? Where is that list?
qs.w: On the new Moby Dick website every old account came over as approved, because the file we had for Moby Dick did not say who was approved and who had only registered. Upper Deck's file did. To fix Moby Dick we need the real list.
opts: The office system (Acctivate) has it: Nicholas or the tech guy pulls the active Moby Dick customers
The old Moby Dick website's user list (Nicholas logs into its admin)
It's the same customers as Upper Deck: use Upper Deck's approved list

sections.title: 3. The family picture: the last eight
sections.lead: Eight questions. The first three make the net worth number solid.

qs.t: Dana Farms, the rental house: what is it worth today, roughly?
qs.w: On the first page it came through as "#25K" against a $240K mortgage, so the number got lost.

qs.t: The life insurance: which policies, on whom, and are the $590K and $900K amounts loans borrowed against the policies?
qs.w: You wrote: one policy 'worth 3.6' with a $590K loan, New York Life worth $1.5M that 'owes $900K', and your Prudential with a $50K loan and $25K owed. These are the two biggest unclear numbers on the whole page.
rows: The '3.6' policy: whose life, which company, and is the $590K a loan against it?
The New York Life policy: whose life, and is the $900K a loan against it?
Your Prudential: is the $25K what's still owed on the $50K loan?

qs.t: 2025 profit: did the wholesale side and the two shops truly clear nothing last year?
qs.w: You wrote "none" for wholesale profit, shop profit, and what you and Dad take out. If that is a true zero, say so; if the question read wrong, give the rough numbers.
rows: Wholesale (Upper Deck + Moby Dick) 2025 profit, rough
What you and Dad lived on in 2025, rough
